title: Streaming metadata may identify the child or household
description: Even if the video payload itself is expected, identifiers or network metadata in transit may enable identification of the child, parent account, or household receiving the stream.
assumptions: Assumes the stream uses account tokens, device IDs, or network attributes that can be tied to an identifiable person or household.
uncertainty_note: Specific I tree node is approximate because the detailed identification tree was not provided.

title: Interception of the stream discloses viewing content and behavior
description: If the stream or its metadata is observable in transit, third parties may learn what approved video is being watched and when, revealing the child's viewing behavior and potentially sensitive preferences.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient transport protection or exposure of meaningful metadata to intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is approximate because the retrieved context did not include the detailed D threat tree.

title: Playback environment may expose the child's viewing to bystanders
description: Once received by the Child User, the streamed video and associated recommendations or titles may be visible or audible to nearby people, disclosing the child's viewing choices or interests.
assumptions: Assumes the child consumes the stream on a shared or observable device/environment.
uncertainty_note: This is a contextual destination-side disclosure threat; applicability depends on the modeled scope including the recipient environment.

title: Streaming and logging of children's viewing data may violate data-minimization or child-privacy obligations
description: Delivering the stream may involve processing and logging children's viewing history, timestamps, device identifiers, or account associations. If this exceeds what is necessary for delivery, lacks an appropriate legal basis/consent, or is retained too long, the flow can contribute to non-compliance with child-privacy and data-protection requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the service logs or otherwise stores delivery-related personal data about child viewers.

title: Excessive disclosure of child browsing data from profiles store
description: The childprofiles collection may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary when sending browsing data to the AI Recommendation Engine. Because the data concerns children and browsing behavior, unnecessary attributes, historical records, or identifiers could be transferred even if the recommendation task only needs a reduced feature set.
assumptions: Assumes the planned integration may send raw or broad child profile/browsing records rather than a minimized subset required for recommendation generation.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; the retrieved context confirms Dd applicability but not the exact subtree citation.

title: AI engine may use received child browsing data beyond the original recommendation purpose
description: Once the AI Recommendation Engine receives child browsing data, it may process, retain, or expose that data for secondary purposes such as model training, profiling enrichment, analytics, or debugging beyond what is necessary for generating recommendations. This constitutes avoidable disclosure at the destination because the recipient's handling expands who or what can learn personal information.
assumptions: Assumes P4 may store inputs, logs, features, or training artifacts, or otherwise reuse incoming data beyond immediate inference.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; threat applicability is strong given planned transfer of children's browsing data to an AI component.

title: Unawareness of AI-based use of child browsing data
description: Data subjects or their guardians may be unaware that browsing data stored in the childprofiles collection is sent to an AI Recommendation Engine and used to generate recommendations or profiles. The planned nature of the flow suggests a risk that this use is not yet transparently communicated or made understandable.
assumptions: Assumes notices, parental information, or in-product explanations may not clearly describe this AI processing activity.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort; retrieved context did not include the unawareness subtree.

title: Processing child browsing data for AI recommendations without valid consent or appropriate legal basis
description: Using child browsing data in an AI Recommendation Engine may require explicit parental consent or another valid legal basis, especially if the processing is not strictly necessary for service delivery or involves profiling. If the engine consumes this data before such authorization is obtained or enforced, the flow creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the system operates in a jurisdiction where children's profiling/recommendation uses require heightened safeguards, transparency, and possibly parental consent.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate, but the compliance risk is genuine because the data concerns children and AI-driven profiling/recommendation.

title: AI engine can identify a child from transferred browsing data
description: If the transferred browsing data includes direct identifiers, persistent account identifiers, device-linked identifiers, or sufficiently unique behavioral patterns, the AI Recommendation Engine may be able to identify or single out a specific child. Identification risk arises at the destination because P4 receives and can combine the data for identity resolution.
assumptions: Assumes browsing data is linked to child profiles or contains stable identifiers or highly distinctive behavior.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; applicability depends on whether identifiers or unique patterns are included in the payload.

title: AI engine may link child browsing data with other datasets or model features
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may link incoming browsing data from the childprofiles collection with other internal datasets, recommendation histories, account data, or learned feature stores, enabling a more complete profile of the child. This increases privacy risk by connecting records that were previously separate.
assumptions: Assumes P4 has access to additional user, content, telemetry, or model-training datasets that can be correlated with the incoming flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort; retrieved context did not include the linkability subtree.

title: Unnecessary sharing of browsing data with third-party advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine plans to disclose users' browsing data to third-party advertisers. This is a cross-boundary transfer of personal data to a third party and may exceed what is strictly necessary for providing recommendations, creating an avoidable explicit data disclosure threat.
assumptions: Browsing data relates to identifiable or reasonably linkable users and is not strictly necessary to be shared with advertisers for the core service requested by the user.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for explicit/avoidable third-party disclosure; exact sub-node naming may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Advertisers can link browsing data to existing profiles
description: Upon receipt, third-party advertisers may combine the browsing data with their own identifiers, cookies, device fingerprints, or customer records to link this flow's data to the same individual across services and contexts.
assumptions: Advertisers possess other identifiers or datasets enabling correlation.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; threat applicability is strong even if sub-node numbering differs.

title: Advertisers may identify users from browsing data
description: The received browsing data may directly identify users or make them identifiable when combined with other data held by advertisers, revealing the user's identity behind the behavioral data.
assumptions: Browsing data contains direct identifiers, persistent pseudonyms, or sufficiently unique behavioral patterns.
uncertainty_note: Identification depends on the granularity of the browsing data and advertiser-side auxiliary data.

title: Advertisers can infer sensitive interests from browsing behavior
description: Browsing histories and interaction patterns can reveal or strongly suggest sensitive attributes such as health concerns, political views, religion, sexuality, financial status, or other private interests once processed by advertisers.
assumptions: The shared browsing data is granular enough to support profiling or inference.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node numbering is approximate; disclosure/content unawareness may also be relevant depending on notice provided.

title: Users may be unaware that browsing data is shared for advertising
description: If users are not clearly informed that their browsing data will be sent to third-party advertisers, they may be unaware of this secondary use and its privacy consequences.
assumptions: Transparency notices are absent, unclear, or not presented at the time of collection/use.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on the actual notice/UX design, which is not provided in the flow description.

title: Sharing browsing data with advertisers may occur without valid consent or other legal basis
description: Sending browsing data to third-party advertisers for advertising purposes may require specific, informed, and freely given consent or another valid legal basis. If that basis is missing, invalid, or not demonstrable, the flow creates a non-compliance threat.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy requires consent or another legal basis for this advertising disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Legal applicability varies by jurisdiction and implementation details; exact node numbering is approximate.

title: Excessive collection/storage of government ID images
description: The Authentication Service stores full government ID images in the file system. Because government ID images are highly sensitive personal data and often contain more attributes than strictly necessary for authentication, this flow may disclose more personal data to the system than needed, violating data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes the service could achieve its purpose with less data, e.g. extracted attributes, redacted images, or short-lived processing instead of persistent storage.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimization structure; exact subnode may differ by catalog version.

title: Persistent retention of ID images in backend file storage
description: On receipt, the file system stores government ID images, creating a risk of avoidable disclosure through unnecessary retention. Keeping raw ID images in backend/uploads/ increases exposure of sensitive personal data beyond the immediate verification need.
assumptions: Assumes retention limits, deletion, or safer storage patterns are not enforced or may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node id is approximate; threat is grounded in avoidable storage/retention of sensitive personal data at the destination.

title: Government ID images in transit can directly identify the individual
description: The data flow carries raw government ID images, which typically contain direct identifiers such as name, photo, document number, date of birth, and address. Anyone able to observe or intercept the flow could identify the data subject from the content itself.
uncertainty_note: Applies if the transfer path is observable to unauthorized parties; exact tree node id is best-effort.

title: Uploads can link a user's identity-verification event to stored account activity
description: Because the flow transfers a government ID image from the Authentication Service to a specific backend upload location, the event and associated metadata can link a particular user account or session to a real-world identity document. This enables correlation between identity-verification activity and other records handled by the system.
assumptions: Assumes flow metadata, filenames, paths, timestamps, or associated application context can be correlated with user/account records.
uncertainty_note: Linkability depends on surrounding metadata and naming conventions; exact tree node id is approximate.

title: Storage of raw ID images may be unexpected by users
description: If users expect their ID to be checked transiently but the system stores the raw image in backend/uploads/, the destination processing may be insufficiently transparent and therefore unexpected. This undermines users' awareness of how their sensitive identity documents are handled.
assumptions: Assumes notices or consent flows do not clearly explain persistent storage of raw ID images.
uncertainty_note: This is an unawareness threat only if transparency about storage is lacking; exact tree node id is approximate.

title: Storing ID images may exceed or diverge from the stated verification purpose
description: Once government ID images are stored in the file system, they may be available for later reuse, secondary processing, or retention beyond the original authentication purpose. If this storage is not necessary for the declared purpose, the destination processing creates a non-compliance risk with purpose limitation and storage limitation obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the declared purpose is identity verification/authentication rather than long-term archival of raw ID images.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node id is approximate; applicability depends on the system's stated purpose and retention policy.

title: JWT in localStorage enables cross-context linkability within the browser
description: Storing a persistent JWT in browser localStorage allows the same token to be reused across sessions and application states on the same origin. Scripts executing in that origin can read the token and correlate a user's actions over time, making separate visits or activities linkable.
assumptions: The JWT is long-lived or reused across multiple requests/sessions and is accessible to application scripts on the same origin.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on general LINDDUN linkability taxonomy; exact node numbering may vary by version.

title: JWT stored in localStorage can identify the user to scripts with access
description: A JWT commonly contains stable identifiers or claims about the user, or functions as a bearer identifier even when opaque. Once stored in localStorage, any script running in the origin can read it and identify the user or single them out.
assumptions: The JWT contains identifying claims or is usable as a stable bearer token tied to one account.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; applicability is strong because localStorage is script-accessible.

title: JWT contents in localStorage may disclose personal data
description: If the JWT payload includes personal attributes, roles, email address, subject identifiers, or other claims, storing it in localStorage exposes that information to any script with origin access, increasing the risk of unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: The JWT is not encrypted end-to-end for storage and contains readable claims with personal or sensitive information.
uncertainty_note: Applies only if the token contains readable personal data; many JWTs do.

title: Users may be unaware that authentication tokens persist in localStorage
description: Persisting a JWT in localStorage can create hidden, durable authentication state. Users may not understand that closing the browser or logging out incompletely may leave the token stored, reducing predictability and intervenability over how long authentication data remains on the device.
assumptions: The application does not clearly inform users about token persistence, retention, and logout/removal behavior.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; threat is grounded in lack of user awareness/control over persistent client-side storage.

title: Storing JWT in localStorage may conflict with data-minimization and secure-storage expectations
description: Persisting a bearer token in localStorage may violate privacy/security requirements or internal policies that require minimizing client-side storage of authentication data, limiting retention, or using more privacy-preserving storage mechanisms. This can create non-compliance if the token persists longer than necessary or is stored in an insufficiently protected location.
assumptions: Applicable policies, standards, or regulatory obligations require minimizing retention and protecting authentication-related personal data on client devices.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on the system's applicable policy/regulatory context; exact tree-node id is best-effort.

title: Excessive disclosure of child history to parent
description: The Child Profile Management process may disclose more of the child's history than is necessary for the parent's immediate review purpose, revealing sensitive behavioral, educational, or health-related details beyond what is proportionate.
assumptions: Assumes the retrieved child history can contain sensitive or extensive records and that not all of it is strictly necessary for each review interaction.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement for disclosure at the source; exact sub-node may differ in the project’s threat-tree version.

title: Child identifiable information exposed in transit
description: The flow carrying child history to the parent can contain direct identifiers or quasi-identifiers about the child, making the child identifiable from the transmitted content or associated metadata if observed in transit.
assumptions: Assumes the history includes identifiers, timestamps, unique events, or other attributes that can single out the child.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transport protection or minimization is insufficient; exact node id may vary by threat-tree edition.

title: Linkability through repeated history-review transmissions
description: Repeated transmissions of child history and their metadata (such as parent account, child reference, timestamps, and review patterns) may allow linking multiple interactions into a detailed profile of the child and family over time.
assumptions: Assumes recurring identifiers or stable metadata are present across requests/responses.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement node selection; the general linking threat clearly applies even if the exact sub-node label differs.

title: Further disclosure by the parent after receipt
description: Once the parent receives the child history, the information may be stored, shared, screenshotted, or shown onward in ways that exceed the original intended context, causing additional privacy disclosure about the child.
assumptions: Assumes the external entity can retain or redistribute the received history outside system controls.
uncertainty_note: This is a destination-side disclosure threat grounded in recipient handling; exact sub-node may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency to the child about parental access
description: The child may not be adequately informed that their history is being retrieved and presented to the parent, including what categories of history are shared and under what conditions, undermining transparency and awareness.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not clearly communicate parental review access to the child data subject.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on applicable transparency obligations and product context; exact node id is best judgement.

title: Unawareness due to opaque retrieval logic
description: The process may provide child history to the parent without mechanisms that let the affected child understand what was retrieved, why it was shared, or whether filtering/redaction was applied, leaving the data subject unaware of processing.
assumptions: Assumes the child is a relevant data subject and the system lacks suitable notices or explanations.
uncertainty_note: Potential overlap with transparency/non-compliance; included here only insofar as user unawareness is a distinct privacy harm.
